faq.q: How far is Sotogrande from Puerto Banús by boat?
faq.a: The distance from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande Marina is about 15 nautical miles. A motor yacht at cruising speed covers it in 30–45 minutes, depending on sea conditions and vessel. Our fleet departs directly from Puerto Banús, making it a quick and scenic coastal run.

faq.q: Can I watch the polo final from the boat?
faq.a: You can anchor near Sotogrande's coastline and watch the match from the water, but for the full experience we recommend docking at Sotogrande Marina (subject to availability) and walking to the Santa María Polo Club. The marina is a 5-minute walk from the club entrance.

faq.q: What boat is best for a group of 12 going to the polo final?
faq.a: For 12 passengers, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) or Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) are ideal. The Mangusta 80 includes a free jet ski and costs €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours. Both depart from Puerto Banús and offer ample deck space for the trip.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to rent a boat for the whole day or just for the polo trip?
faq.a: If you only want to attend the polo final and return, a 4-hour charter on a Tier A boat (€1,499) or a half-day on a Mangusta 80 (€4,719) works well. For a full day including lunch at sea, our 8-hour Tier A charter is €2,299. Compare options via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Does the boat rental include lunch or catering?
faq.a: All charters include light snacks, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava. For a full meal, you can arrange catering through us in advance (extra cost) or bring your own food. Many guests stop at a chiringuito along the coast for lunch.

faq.q: Can I combine a boat rental with a visit to Estepona or Cabopino?
faq.a: Yes. On the way to Sotogrande, you can stop at Cabopino beach or Estepona port for a swim or lunch. The coastal route from Puerto Banús passes both. A 6–8 hour charter gives you plenty of time for multiple stops.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the polo final day?
faq.a: We monitor forecasts closely. If conditions are unsafe, we offer a full refund or reschedule to another day. The Mediterranean in August is generally calm, with average sea temperatures of 25°C and light winds.

faq.q: How do I book a boat for the Sotogrande polo final?
faq.a: Contact us via WhatsApp with your preferred date, group size, and boat type. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) we can confirm immediately. For other yachts, we'll provide pricing within minutes. A 50% deposit secures the booking.

data.body_html:
The Sotogrande Polo Final 2040 is one of the Costa del Sol's most prestigious summer events, drawing international crowds to the Santa María Polo Club. Combining the match with a Marbella boat rental from Puerto Banús turns the day into a seamless luxury experience: cruise the coast, anchor for a swim, dock at Sotogrande Marina, and walk to the club. With our fleet departing from Puerto Banús, the entire trip is under an hour by sea. This guide covers logistics, boat options, pricing, and tips for making the most of both the polo and the sailing.

Why Combine a Boat Rental with the Polo Final?

The Sotogrande Polo Final 2040 takes place in August, when the Mediterranean is at its warmest (sea temperature around 25°C). A private charter lets you avoid traffic on the AP-7 motorway, arrive in style, and enjoy the coastline before or after the match. You can anchor at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for a swim, stop for lunch at a beach club in Estepona, or simply cruise past the Golden Mile. The boat becomes your mobile base for the day.

Fleet Options for the Trip

We operate from Puerto Banús with a range of motor yachts and speedboats. For a group attending the polo final, here are the most suitable options:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – €749/2h or €2,299/8h, includes skipper, drinks, snacks, and VAT.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – same pricing as Astondoa 40.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – €4,719 minimum 4h, includes free jet ski. Perfect for a larger group wanting extra water toys.
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) – pricing on request via WhatsApp.
  • Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax) – ideal for a sporty, fast transfer.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and a selection of drinks and snacks. For boats not listed in Tier A or B, contact us via WhatsApp for a quote.

Sample Itinerary: Boat + Polo Final

A typical day might look like this:

  • 10:00 – Depart Puerto Banús. Cruise east past Marbella Marina and Cabopino.
  • 10:45 – Arrive at Sotogrande Marina. Walk 5 minutes to Santa María Polo Club.
  • 11:00–14:00 – Watch the polo final (times vary; check the official schedule).
  • 14:00–15:30 – Lunch at a club restaurant or back on the boat with catering.
  • 15:30–17:00 – Cruise back, with a swim stop at Cala del Faro or Estepona.
  • 17:00 – Return to Puerto Banús.

If you prefer a longer day, extend to 8 hours and include a visit to Sotogrande's beach club or a sunset cruise.

Booking Tips for the Polo Final 2040

The Sotogrande Polo Final is a high-demand event. Book your boat at least 2–3 weeks in advance, especially for larger yachts. We recommend a minimum 4-hour charter to allow time for the match and a relaxed cruise. For a full day with lunch and swimming, choose the 8-hour option. Contact us via WhatsApp to check availability for your preferred date.

What to Bring

Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, swimwear, and a light jacket for the evening return. The boat provides towels and snorkelling gear on request. If you plan to eat at the polo club, smart-casual attire is expected. Leave large bags on the boat – the marina is secure.

Nearby Attractions

While in the area, consider extending your trip to Estepona's old town (10 minutes by taxi from the marina) or the dunes of Cabopino. For a longer charter, head west to Gibraltar or east to Nerja. Our skippers know the best anchorages and can tailor the route to your interests.
